thread:
maria (support): heads up — after today's rate-limit policy rollout (v2) we're getting a spike in 429 reports from two mid-market customers and a few internal canary runs. customers reporting intermittent 429s even though they say they didn't exceed quota. :rotating_light:

lee (oncall): copying me. any correlation with region or model?

maria (support): mostly us-east and us-west, models: text-gen-large, text-chat. spikes started ~08:14 UTC, coincides with rollout window. support ticket ids: 7612, 7621.

ash (deploy-bot): deploy finished: rate-policy/v2 -> production (canary 20% -> 100%) by jordan at 08:12 UTC.

lee (oncall): ok can everyone grab the rollout PR and the config? jordan — did the rollout go straight to 100%?

jordan (eng-platform): we ramped from 20% to 100% after green checks from telemetry at ~08:10. Policy changed default per-organization burst window from 60s to 10s and tightened per-second limits. I can paste the snippet: 

```
# rate-policy/v2 snippet
per_second: 50
burst_window_seconds: 10
max_burst_tokens: 500
per_minute: 2000
# previous: burst_window_seconds: 60, max_burst_tokens: 3000
```

jordan (eng-platform): intent was to reduce tail latency by limiting long burst allowances; thought standard workloads would be unaffected.

ash (deploy-bot): canary metrics: 20% -> success, 99th latency OK for requests, error rate low.

ash (deploy-bot): post-100%: error rate increased by 0.7% in production over baseline; 429s up by ~1.8x in last 15m.

ash (deploy-bot): notable: error increase concentrated on customers with per-organization token bucket usage ~500-1500 tokens/min and short spikey traffic patterns.

ash (deploy-bot): logs sample: 
```
{"ts":"2025-09-14T08:16:21Z","org_id":"acme-corp","route":"/v1/generate","status":429,"reason":"quota_exhausted","tokens_requested":320,"tokens_available":0}
```

ash (deploy-bot): also saw a handful of 401s earlier but they were transient and unrelated; nothing in auth service.

ash (deploy-bot): traced a canary client replay: client sends a few large parallel requests that used up burst tokens quickly, then subsequent short requests hit 429 immediately.

ash (deploy-bot): possible that reducing burst_window_seconds from 60->10 reduced available KV TTL for token regeneration in our distributed limiter, leading to short-term bucket starvation under certain concurrency patterns.

ash (deploy-bot): could be implementation subtlety: limiter uses sliding-window approximation that depends on sample alignment across shards — shorter windows amplify race conditions.

lee (oncall): good theory. ashwin, can you reproduce locally with the load generator? steps to repro would help support responses.

ashwin (eng-sre): on it. I'll run an org-sim with the exact policy and a few clients doing: 5 parallel requests each requesting 320 tokens, repeating every 2s for 30s.

ashwin (eng-sre): quick repro confirmed: with v2 policy the clients see sustained 429s after initial burst; with v1 policy the same pattern succeeds until minute boundary. I'll attach raw load profile.

ashwin (eng-sre): stack trace is in limiter service logs: high CAS retries on redis keys for token buckets, and TTLs showing 10s windows causing more frequent refills and race conditions.

lee (oncall): decision time. Options: 1) rollback to v1 immediately; 2) tweak v2 config to increase burst_window_seconds back to something like 30s; 3) add temporary per-org exception for flagged customers; 4) patch limiter code (longer). Rolling back seems safest for customer impact. Thoughts?

jordan (eng-platform): we can rollback quickly. rollback command: 

```bash
./deploy_tool rollback rate-policy/v2 --to rate-policy/v1 --reason "customer 429 spike" --force
```

jordan (eng-platform): I can kick it and monitor.

maria (support): recommend rollback — send a note to affected customers once it's done. katie, can you draft a short note? include apology and that it's a policy configuration issue being rolled back.

katie (customer-success): on it. I'll draft: "We're rollbackling a rate-policy change that caused unexpected 429s for bursty workloads — service should return to normal within minutes. Please reply if you still see issues."

lee (oncall): ashwin — estimate time to rollback + propagation?

ashwin (eng-sre): rollback should be quick, policy update takes ~30s to propagate to edge nodes but watch redis shards for CAS backlog. I'll watch logs and SLO dashboards.

jordan (eng-platform): kicking rollback now.

jordan (eng-platform): ./deploy_tool rollback command submitted — job id 7291.

ashwin (eng-sre): watching job 7291. First edge versions downgrading.

ashwin (eng-sre): metrics: 429 rate dropping in the next 60s. Great.

maria (support): customers reporting fewer 429s already — ticket 7612 updated.

lee (oncall): ok keep monitoring 15m for recurrence. postmortem prep: include repro steps, root cause (short window amplified limiter races), mitigation (rollback + increase canary criteria), and action items (tweak tests, add chaos test).

ashwin (eng-sre): immediate action items I captured: 
- revert rollout to v1 (done)
- add integration test simulating parallel bursty clients against limiter with windows 5s-60s
- add telemetry that exposes per-org token refill CAS failures
- set future canary ramp policy: 20% -> 40% -> 70% -> 100% with 15m observation windows

jordan (eng-platform): I'll open the rollback PR notes and schedule a follow-up to propose a v2.1 with code fix and larger burst window.

katie (customer-success): I sent notes to affected customers and flagged for follow-up tomorrow. One customer asked if this could affect their SLA — I told them we'll follow up and escalate to sales/ops.

lee (oncall): great. don't forget to file an incident ticket and assign severity 2 since this impacted multiple paying customers.

maria (support): filed INC-2025-109 in ops board, linked tickets 7612/7621.

ashwin (eng-sre): final note: small but important lesson — config-only changes to rate machinery can interact with distributed implementation in non-obvious ways. Add a checklist for policy changes: include distributed-limiter regression tests + redis CAS telemetry + longer canary ramp.

lee (oncall): thanks team. closing thread after 15m of clean metrics. :thumbsup:
